descripcion: Zonas de lanzamiento de drones de largo alcance que nombran los partes de la Fuerza Aérea de Ucrania, con las raíces con que aparecen en ellos, su punto (con la fuente que lo da literalmente) y las fuentes que documentan su uso para lanzar drones. Verificado el 2 de octubre de 2026. La coordenada que daba el borrador para Primorsko-Ajtarsk (46°40′34.48″N 38°07′49.75″E) es la del pie de la figura 3 del informe del Institute for Science and International Security (B1), que corresponde al emplazamiento de Yeysk: aquí está en la zona de Yeysk, y Primorsko-Ajtarsk lleva la de su base aérea (B27) y la del puerto de drones cercano (B7). El radio de cada zona como origen no sale de las fuentes: lo pone el motor por tipo (proceso/deduccion/catalogo.py).

uso.cita: However, with the increased use of strike drones, a separate infrastructure for launching UAVs was constructed near the main base. The site includes two areas for storing drones, 24 garage units, a launch strip for mobile launchers, and, most likely, four fixed launchers.

uso.cita: One launch site is situated near the village of Tsymbulovo in the Oryol region, approximately 175 kilometers from the Ukrainian border. It is considered the main droneport for Russia’s long-range UAVs.
The site hosts eight stationary launch platforms and a 2.80 km stretch of road used for launching Shahed drones from vehicles.
According to geolocation analysis by X user Mark Krutov , the launches took place at coordinates 53.37280109648919, 35.80028358981446 —the same facility previously hit by Ukrainian strikes.
The analysts estimate that this is Russia's largest launch site, with a total area exceeding 5 sq km and a launch runway more than 2.5 km long.
